_comment: Completion state for the v1.0 work orders, consumed by tools/gen_tracker.py. States: done | partial | todo | blocked. Record 'done' only with evidence checked into this repo.

AX-001.note: All three leak sites closed (c840f9a). The audit's attribution to `archx_fn___archx_user_main` was wrong; the real defect was in the collection pipeline: (1) comprehension growth (cap==len so the last push reallocated), (2) the min/max generator temp claimed without being freed, (3) the for-each loop variable re-cloned over the previous binding. ASan now 11/11 CLEAN; ci/leakcheck.c is an independent gate that provably fails on a leak.

AX-002.note: Complete. `int` is a trapping i64 end to end: llvm.s{add,sub,mul}.with.overflow plus an immediate (never deferred) trap so a wrapped value is never observable, checked constant folding so a literal cannot bypass the check, checked abs/pow, and a use-gated check so a representable answer never traps (2**40, 2**62, (-2)**63, 1**100, 0**0 all answer). This round closed the two remaining pieces. (1) The explicit opt-out: wrapping_add/wrapping_sub/wrapping_mul for native dialect, folding constants with the same modular semantics, rejected in compat as E0802 (CPython's int is arbitrary precision, so wrapping there would be a wrong answer), and recorded in the artifact as archx.wrapping in the llvm.module.flags so a binary that may wrap is identifiable without its source. (2) The `no add nsw without a proof` audit found two REAL UB hazards and one REAL correctness bug: integer true division computed |x| with `sub nsw i64 0, x`, which is poison for i64::MIN — so LLVM could delete the branch reading it and drop the >2^53 correction term for exactly that operand; now a total sign-split comparison, no negation at all. hex/oct/bin had the same unconditional nsw negation on a user value; now a plain sub (its bit pattern IS the unsigned magnitude the urem loop wants). And while verifying that, the digit-selection bug surfaced: the loop chose a letter when the BASE was 16 rather than when the DIGIT was >= 10, so hex(1) printed `0xX` and hex(16) `0xXW` — every small non-letter value was wrong; fixed in both @archx_int_to_base_str and @archx_int_to_base_raw, and pinned by a new conformance probe (num_base_str_values) covering 0..16, 255, 4095, negatives, i64::MIN/MAX and :x/:X/:o/:b format specs. Unjustified nsw/nuw was also removed from the list-copy and search loops, and the one remaining nsw (region repeat) now documents the check that proves it.

AX-003.note: Version single-sourced: Cargo.toml 0.9.0 -> 0.9.1 (the CLI already read CARGO_PKG_VERSION; `archx --version` now prints 0.9.1) and benchmarks/run.sh now derives every version string from Cargo.toml instead of hard-coding 0.9.0. The README benchmark table is GENERATED from ci/out/benchmarks.txt by tools/sync_readme_benchmarks.py, which also rewrites the two perf claims; `--check` fails on drift and was verified to fail on an injected stale number. tools/check_test_count.py asserts the quoted count equals the `#[test]` attributes (79 = 41 unit + 38 CLI; the old 68 was stale). "(Current)" removed from the v0.8.0 changerog heading. Both checks run in CI. HONESTY FIX: the old claim `4.1x-69.8x faster than Python 3` silently omitted Suite 1 where Archx is 0.3x; the range is now `4.0x-71.2x` over Suites 2-7 with the Suite 1 loss stated in the same sentence, and the full_tour sentence no longer says it beats C (the CI run has C at 12 ms vs Archx 17 ms).

AX-005.note: LICENSE (MIT) added earlier. The binary problem was larger than the work order described: SIX tracked executables, not two (`bw`, `call_and_loop_semantics`, `d1`, `full_tour_pythonic`, `hello`, `pipelines`) — the other four are build output from `benchmarks/run.sh` that was committed by accident. All six are removed from the index and ignored by name; `tools/check_binaries.py` scans the magic number of every tracked blob (so it needs no `file(1)` and cannot miss an extensionless binary), is wired into CI, and was verified to fail on a planted ELF before being trusted. Acceptance met: zero ELF/Mach-O/PE files tracked.

AX-006.note: Needs a decision I cannot make alone: merging arena/888b3ea8-archx-lang into `main` and changing the default branch is a repo-level action affecting what `git clone` gives everyone. Depends on AX-003 and AX-005 landing first.

AX-013.note: Directive layer landed (b152f3b): src/dialect.rs, E0100/E0101, DialectSpec on Program, --dialect override. ACCEPTANCE PARTLY MET: `--emit-ir` now carries the dialect as llvm.module.flags (`archx.dialect` + `archx.directive_version`, behaviour bit 1 = Error), asserted by tests/cli.rs::dialect_directive_is_required_and_checked for both dialects. REMAINING: `NodeOrigin { dialect, span }` on Stmt/Expr (needs per-node spans, a larger change) — and `DialectRules` was removed because no pass read it; AX-016 reintroduces the table as the thing passes actually consult.

AX-004.note: All 15 warnings resolved and the gate is in CI. Dead code deleted (not allowed): `emit_pack_dict_key`, `clauses_carry`, `param_as_expr`, `declare_loop_var_in_outer_scope`, `forget_drop_target`, plus the never-constructed `StmtKind::ForElse` (AX-010). Unread parameters removed from signatures (`arr_name` in `emit_list_push_raw`/`emit_list_scan_var`, `span` in `gen_for`, `gen_foreach`, `gen_for_else`, `gen_foreach_else`), unused `mut`s dropped. `#[deny(dead_code)]` on `mod ast`. CI runs `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build --all-targets` on Linux and on both cross-platform runners; local release + all-targets builds are clean. NOTE: the acceptance text says `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`; the tree has never been clippy-clean (65 lints, incl. 27 `map_or` style suggestions), so the gate is rustc warnings. Clippy-clean is left as separate work rather than silently claimed.

AX-010.note: `StmtKind::ForElse` deleted from src/ast.rs: `For`, `ForEach`, `ForEnumerate`, `ForDictItems`, `ForZip`, `ForTupleUnpack` already each carry `else_body: Option<Vec<Stmt>>` and every one of them is constructed by the parser, so the variant was a second, unreachable representation. Its arms were removed from codegen/analysis.rs, codegen/mod.rs, codegen/generics.rs, codegen/stmt.rs and parser.rs. Acceptance met: one representation, loop tests unchanged and green (41 unit + 38 CLI).

AX-009.note: ci/verify_ir.sh lowers every example, every benchmark and a targeted runtime corpus and passes each module to clang -c (a real LLVM parse + verify); it is wired into CI and currently verifies 29 modules with 0 failures. The corpus that reaches every runtime subsystem (ints/floats, %ArchxAny incl. the binop helper that was broken, dict/set, regions, SoA structs, tuples/enums/match, comprehensions/sort/zip/generics, input/assert) lives once in src/codegen/tests.rs::RUNTIME_CORPUS, is lowered by the unit test every_runtime_feature_lowers_to_ir, and is written to ci/out/runtime-corpus/ for the shell gate. The gate was proven to fail on a planted bad phi predecessor (the exact v0.9.1 bug shape) before being trusted. NOTE: `llvm-as`/`opt` are not installed in the development sandbox or on the CI images' default PATH, so the frontend is clang's IR parser/verifier, not llvm-as.

AX-012.note: ci/reproducibility.sh compiles every benchmark and example TWICE and requires byte-identical emitted IR and byte-identical linked binaries, plus a third compilation in a separate process with a different hash seed and MALLOC_PERTURB_, and byte-identical stdout AND stderr between the two builds; wired into CI next to the IR verifier. Running it first found two real defects: (1) monomorphized Func/StructDef and lifted closures were collected in HashMaps and appended with into_values(), so the order of `define` blocks changed per run and, because LLVM lays out code in input order, so did the binaries — now BTreeMaps (src/codegen/generics.rs); (2) clang names the object's file symbol after its input file, and the input was `$TMP/archx-<pid>-<n>.ll`, so every binary embedded a different sandbox path — the module now carries `source_filename = "<real source name>"` via codegen::lower_with_source, which also makes --emit-ir self-describing. Toolchain is recorded in ci/logs/toolchain.log each run (rustc, cargo, clang, and clang's default target); the installed toolchain is the newest available in this environment: rustc 1.97.0, clang 22.1.8.

AX-007.note: tests/conformance/ holds 104 probes, each ONE file that is legal Python and legal Archx (line 1 is the directive, which Python reads as a comment), so the same bytes are executed by python3 and compiled by archx; tests/conformance.rs compares stdout byte-for-byte, writes tests/conformance/conformance.md, and is wired into CI. A probe can only be xfailed with a mandatory reason (`# conformance: xfail <reason>`), and an xfail probe that starts passing fails the run so the limitations list cannot go stale. Result: 64 of 104 match CPython, 40 documented gaps, 0 undocumented divergences. The harness immediately found two REAL compat-contract violations, now fixed: compat printed `true`/`false` instead of `True`/`False`, and container elements were printed without `repr()` quotes (`[a, b]` instead of `['a', 'b']`). Both are dialect-gated (Dialect::bool_words / Dialect::container_repr) and verified in native and compat. NOTE: the original 123 audit probes were in a lost temp upload, so this probe set was written fresh rather than pretending to reproduce that exact corpus.

AX-008.note: docs/LIMITATIONS.md is GENERATED by tools/gen_limitations.py from the xfail markers in tests/conformance/, so every entry maps to a probe that measures it; `--check` in CI fails on drift, and the README links it. Lists 40 gaps by area plus the two deliberate-by-contract divergences (trapping i64, errors trap instead of raising) and the Linux-only leak gate.

AX-011.note: Every diagnostic now carries a stable code from a closed registry of 37 codes in src/error_codes.rs, each with a summary and a full explanation; codes are grouped by area (E00xx driver, E01xx dialect, E02xx lexing, E03xx parsing, E04xx types/calls, E05xx names, E06xx collections, E07xx control flow, E08xx dialect, E09xx internal). Attaching a code at each of ~460 construction sites was the wrong shape, so the MESSAGE stays the authority and src/diagnose.rs owns one ordered table mapping message templates to codes; tests/error_codes.rs reads the compiler's own source, extracts every Diagnostic::new/format! literal and FAILS if any of them does not classify, so a new diagnostic cannot ship uncoded — that gate passes on all 464 literals today. Human output is rustc-style (`error[E0402]: …` plus span and caret) and every driver error (bad flag, unreadable file, clang missing, temp-file failure, clobbering -o) has a code too. `--message-format=json` emits one JSON object per line (hand-rolled escaper, no dependencies; asserted parseable in CI) and `archx explain [CODE]` documents every code. docs/ERROR_CODES.md is generated by tools/gen_error_codes.py from `archx --explain` with a --check drift gate in CI. NOTE: the registry is hand-mapped, so a *reworded* message needs its rule updated — the coverage test catches a missing rule, not a mis-assigned one; the classification tests pin the representative messages of each area.

AX-014.note: The directive layer (src/dialect.rs) accepts `# archx: dialect=compat|native, version=1` as the first line (field order and spacing free, `#archx:` accepted, `version` must be 1), `--dialect` overrides a present directive and the IR records source=cli, and a missing directive is E0100 while a malformed one is E0101. The file extension is only a hint and never selects the contract. This round closed the two gaps the acceptance criteria name. (1) AMBIGUITY: a second directive was silently ignored, so `# archx: dialect=native` followed by a leftover `# archx: dialect=compat` compiled as native with no signal — now E0101 pointing at line 2, and rejected even when the two agree so a stale header cannot survive until it diverges (a line carrying the `# archx:` sigil is always treated as a directive, because the sigil is reserved). (2) FIX-IT: E0100 suggests the exact line to insert when — and only when — the source uses a native-only construct (`struct`, `enum`, `region:`, `with region`, `pub fn`), since then `dialect=native` is the only possible answer; a module that either dialect could compile gets the neutral message and no pasteable guess. tests/cli.rs::dialect_directive_is_unambiguous_and_its_suggestion_is_sound asserts all of it end to end (conflicting and agreeing duplicates, the suggested line, the neutral case, and --dialect recorded as source=cli in the module flags).

AX-016.note: New src/dialect_rules.rs holds the divergence matrix as data: ROWS, one row per Rule with the compat value, the native value, and an `enforced` flag. Consumers read a row through dialect_rules::value(rule, dialect) instead of testing the enum, and the three decisions that used to be scattered in the backend were moved onto it: Dialect::bool_words and Dialect::container_repr are now thin reads of the BoolRepr and ContainerRepr rows (they were `match`es in dialect.rs), and the wrapping opt-out in codegen/calls.rs asks the WrappingOptOut row instead of comparing to Dialect::Native. 8 rules are listed (int overflow, bool repr, container repr, wrapping opt-out, int division, str index unit, mixed numeric arithmetic, runtime failure) and the matrix reports 6 of 8 as genuinely divergent; the other two are listed because readers ask about them and their answers coincide today, which a test asserts so the classification cannot rot. Honesty over completeness: a row is marked `planned` unless a call site really enforces it, so the four not-yet-implemented rows (str indexing by code point, int/float widening, int division as int, exceptions instead of traps) say so rather than claiming completion. `archx --dialect-matrix` prints the table and docs/DIALECTS.md is generated from that output by tools/gen_dialect_matrix.py with a --check drift gate in CI, so the document and the backend are the same object. tests/cli.rs::dialect_matrix_is_the_table_the_compiler_obeys pins both the enforced and the planned verdicts.
